utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, you answered my question. Now we see it on the screen, beginning from line 16. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I think that clears it up. Dragan Todorovic is a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment. The reference was that Mr. Erdemovic was saying this. That is what confused everyone. And as long as it is clear that this is the testimony of Dragan Todorovic, I think Mr. Erdemovic should be able to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, could you help us with an answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not familiar with this name Dragan Todorovic. Was he in the 10th Sabotage Detachment or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not entitled to tell you anything that would suggest the answer to you. If you know something, fine; if you don't, just say so. He was just an OTP witness, and the Prosecution knows who and what he was. I'm just asking you if it is possible that there could be such a confusion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I would object to him instructing the witness on what he can and it cannot say. And also the -- I think the law is clear he may ask a leading question where he is suggesting an answer to the witness, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey I'm -- I don't agree with you. He was -- it was an open question and the witness is capable to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If there is something unclear, you should deal with that in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: My objection was based on him talking to the witness and saying what he could or could not say to him, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: He -- no, I don't agree, Mr. McCloskey. He said to him, If you don't know then just say I don't know. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise that I told the witness that I couldn't tell him because I'm not the one who can provide information. I am the one who is asking questions. That is all. I did not wish to say anything else and I did not wish to involve the witness into anything that would induce him to say one thing or another.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Erdemovic. It is sufficient for me that you said you do not know Mr. Dragan Todorovic. I have no need to ask you anything else about him. We shall move on to the next set of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I just was not looking at you because I tried to figure out what was the correct question of Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand I am -- I am -- I just want to clear up one area of law, and we, perhaps, don't need to do in front of the witness, but Mr. Tolimir perhaps he should get an instruction later that he does have the right, as a cross-examiner, to put information to the witness. And he should know that because it is a fundamental right that he has, and I don't know if that was reflected in his knowledge or that was just a comment he made. But he -- he perhaps -- Your Honours will want to instruct him that he can say, It is our position, based on the evidence, that you were a sergeant. He can provide information. That is a fundamental right he has in asking leading questions to a witness, and I just want to make sure that he know this is early in the case, and I apologise for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. McCloskey. Perhaps I misunderstood you. And, therefore, I'm -- I appreciate your explanation, that clarifies the situation. And I think Mr. Tolimir knows about his rights and will be able to deal with this. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I wish to apologise to you. I did not want to ask any further questions because I received an answer. I do not expect any cunning answers from you. I expect frank answers, and this is why I asked a frank question. So thank you. My next question is this: Did you voluntarily go on mission on the 15th of July 1995, did you volunteer for that or were you assigned to do that? Please tell us how that happened.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Our unit was accommodated in the barracks in Bijeljina as I said. You mentioned the contract that we signed in February of 1995. I cannot see it in front of me, but I know that I signed the contract. I don't remember the exact date. We had a normal working day, from 8.00 a.m. till 5.00 p.m. We had to go to the barracks and spend the whole day there. And, of course, when there was an action, then we had to be on alert 24 hours, and it was like that with those who were appointed as duty officers and duty personnel on a particular day, then it was the same with them. On that day, on the 10th of July, 1995, we arrived to the barracks just on any other normal day. We were then told to go home and take a uniform that we should change into uniform and come back in half an hour because we would be going into action. They did not tell us particularly what action that would be, but I remember that I went home and took some personal hygiene items and I returned to the barracks. Not long after that, we set off in the direction of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes. Please explain that to us in your own words. Let me not interrupt you. The question was: How did you come to go to Srebrenica. So explain everything that you think is necessary. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As I already said, when we came to the barracks in the morning, Franc Kos told to us go home and fetch the personnel hygiene items and an extra uniform because we would go into action. He did not tell us at the time where the action would take place. That's what I can say, that we were issued such an order on that day in the morning that we would be going into action.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to interrupt you very shortly. We had two different dates on the records. Page 60 line 14 in your question, you were referring to the 15th of July, 1995. And I would like to know from the -- if the witness could indicate, is he talking about the 15th or the 10th of July, as indicated on line 25 of the same page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was on the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, for pointing out the error in transcript. It is possible that I said the 15th of July instead of 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let me quote once again this Mr. Todorovic, who was an OTP witness. And he was a sort of company commander in your platoon. And the document is page 2, and the page of transcript is 14041, line 25. And page of transcript 14042, where asked by Prosecutor McCloskey -- this is the question, I'm quoting: "You noticed that Drazen Erdemovic joined this group later. Can you tell us something more about it? What were the circumstances under which Erdemovic was a member of the group?" And Witness Todorovic answers: "Well, he did not want to stay on his own at the base. The Intervention Platoon had already left. Some of the units were having free time, and they were on furlough. Instead of going to Bijeljina on his own, he joined the group that left the base." I apologise to interpreters. I will mention again the last sentence: "Well, he didn't want to stay on his own in the base. The Intervention Squad had already left. Some of the troops were on furlough. Instead of going to Bijeljina on his own, he joined the group that left the base." And my question is this: Mr. Erdemovic, can you please comment on the statement of this Todorovic, whom you say you don't know, and whether it is truthful or not? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what is discussed here, what was the event, what base? Which base? And let me say that, again, the name Dragan Todorovic means nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, in this transcript, there was talk of the 15th of July. So that was after the funeral when you were supposed to go to Srebrenica again. Is that true or not? I have assisted you now because I have told you that the date here was the 15th of July when you were supposed to go there again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I really do not understand what this is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. That was a Prosecution witness, and what he said probably served some other purpose in another case. So did you go with your unit to Srebrenica simultaneously or not? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he issued the order when you can see my name and the names of other persons from my unit, the Bijeljina Platoon. You can see that we all went together, because the order was issued to everyone, and we all left together on that day. I don't understand what this person, this Dragan Todorovic is talking about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I do not wish to be tiresome with Dragan Todorovic. Just tell me, did you go to Srebrenica together with everyone else, or did you come later? This is the only thing that I'm interested in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went together with everyone else on a bus that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In an interview given by your commander, Misa, from the 10th Sabotage Detachment, in November 1955 [as interpreted] on page 7, paragraph 2, that was the weekly "Nin," this is what he says. I'm quoting and I will ask you if this is true or not, what he says there and you remember well, so please see. In November 1995, that is 1D119 so that you and others could follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could Mr. Tolimir be clear on who Misa is so everyone knows who Misa is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I said your commander Misa. I think that it is known who the commander was and Mr. Erdemovic said already who the commander of his unit was. So I said, did you read -- I'm quoting part of the interview which Mr. Pelemis gave to the weekly "Nin." The document is 1D119 on page 7, paragraph 2. Could you please pull that up on it's screen and for Mr. McCloskey, the answer is that it was Misa Pelemis who was the commander. Thank you. Thank you I will now quote. In English it is page 7, paragraph 2, "In November --" I'm quoting from his interview. "In November 1995 --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Wait a moment, please. You should indicate for the witness which part of this interview and the newspaper you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have said page 7, paragraph 2, it givens with the words: "In November 1995 ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you please indicate where in this article in B/C/S, the witness can find it and then it could be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My assistants will see where it is because the font is very small. So they will tell you what line it is. And in the English version, it's page 7, paragraph 2. Page 7, paragraph 2. I cannot read English, so ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tolimir, but the article was not from 1995 but from 2005, from what I can see here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, the article was published in 2005, but it talks about 1995 and I'm quoting him. He says: "In November 1995, I sent a letter to the Main Command that the man is to be sent to a psychiatric ward." In B/C/S, it is the second page and the third column: "He had shown before," and then there's something that is not clear, "most probably because of the actions he had had. The average was two or three actions and he had already had six, seven actions. He volunteered."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is this: Do you know that this is what your commander said about you in the press, and is it true or not? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: This is not true, but, on the other hand, I would not be surprised by anything coming from this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We need our second break. I was waiting for a convenient time, but now it's at the latest point. We must have our second break now. And we will resume at quarter past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We apologise for the late return. We were occupied by another commitment. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We will now move to a different group of questions. I would kindly ask you to tell me the following: Before the attack on Srebrenica, before the arrival in Srebrenica before combat operations, did you receive an order informing that you should not fire into civilians, not set houses on fire, and so on. We've used up a lot of time. I don't want to quote everything now. But please tell me this.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Who issued the order to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Commander of our unit, Pelemis, Milorad Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, what exactly did Pelemis tell you as the commander and did you abide by that while in combat in Srebrenica and around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Commander Pelemis told us we shouldn't shoot at civilians, that we should call civilians to leave their homes and that we should directly them to walk in front of us towards the football stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: All right. And did you act in accordance with that during combat?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In order to be fully fair to Pelemis, I will quote his transcript. Lines 17 to 19, page 10345. Page 10945 and lines 17 to 19 as well. I'm quoting: "As I have said, we should not shoot without reason. We should call upon people to leave their homes. He told us not shoot at civilians. We were told that we can expect great resistance and that we were the first unit to enter the town." I apologise the interpreters. I wanted to conclude this as quickly as possible. My question is: Is it true what I have just read? Is that how he said it to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I must confess, I'm lost. I don't know which page. We have two different references here. Could you indicate again the page number of which transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Transcript 10945, lines 17 to 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 1D119 which is the interview given by Pelemis as commander of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, on the 22nd of September, 2005, for the weekly "Nin" from Belgrade. I will quote what he said there. I'm quoting. We can see it on the screen now: "I have to say that there were no hints for what was going to follow later and Erdemovic confirmed that. I lined up all my people and I explained to them that none of them should set any houses on fire. All civilians and war prisoners need to be kept safe at the centre of Srebrenica at the sports stadium there."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is: Is it true that Pelemis said this, is it true that he lined you up and told you what I have just read out to you now? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Erdemovic. Since we are skipping over some questions so as not to keep you here tomorrow, tell me, please, were there any NATO strikes against you at Srebrenica while you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know whether they hit any of the targets? Are you aware of any such instances?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, when we were at the entrance into town, when we were in a suburb, as I learned later, they did hit the area close to the house where the command of the Drina Wolves were and Deliko [phoen] was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, when was Pelemis injured and when was your colleague killed, the one whose funeral you attended?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you receive an order on the 12th of July telling you that you had leave until the 21st of July?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see 1D119, the penultimate paragraph. Perhaps this would help the witness give his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which page and column in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D119, page 2, penultimate paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PELEMIS SAID
utterances.text: "On the 12th, in the morning, we were given an order informing us that we were on leave until the 21st of July."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't have that on the screen, I think. We have the right document but perhaps not the right paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serbian version needs to be moved so that we see the entire page. This is 1D119, page 2, penultimate paragraph, where it says and I'm quoting: "On the 12th, in the morning, we were given an order informing us that we were on leave until the 21st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Tell us, please, until what time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... [Microphone not activated] we have the right document but ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move the document to the left so that we can see the Serbian version. And it's page 4 in the English. All right. We can see it now here in the first column, third bullet reads, I'm quoting: "On the 12th, in the morning, at about 10.00, 11.00, we received an order that we were on leave until the 21st of July. About 3.00 or 4.00 p.m. on the 12th, we withdrew along the Srebrenica-Milic-Vlasenica axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Sir, what I just read out, is it true and were you really on leave after your friend was killed so that you could attend his funeral?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't on leave. I was designated to go and attend the funeral in Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: All right. Well, that's what I said. You were on leave in the sense that you didn't have to participate in combat operations, so you went to the funeral and when did you come back?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Which came in the morning on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In this interview your commander says that he was injured and that he was on sick-leave and on treatment. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When exactly was he on sick-leave?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: After that event and -- during the funeral -- or, rather, did he attend the funeral with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. He did not attend the funeral. And on the 16th in the morning, he was present at Dragasevac, at the headquarters of the Vlasenica Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution showed two documents here. One is the document they showed for an earlier witness, 008690096 in e-court. And it's 4037 on the OTP 65 ter list. Could we pull that document on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you tendering the last document, the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. Could that be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would object to that, Mr. President, as a violation of the rules required by 92 bis and the other rules. And it's a newspaper interview so its reliability to the Court shouldn't be much. And this person is available and perhaps could be called as witness. He may be available, but I know he is alive and well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We will deal with that later, not to waste the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I simply wanted to tender into evidence the document that I put to the witness here, and this document speaks about his unit and the events in which he participated, and it's up to the Court to decide whether it will be admitted or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We will deal with that later. We have now the document you were asking for on the screen, and please continue and put questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, I will now read out from a document which was OTP 65 ter 4037. Please listen to this, and I will put my question later: "The President of Republika Srpska was informed of successful combat operations around Srebrenica by units of the Drina Corps and that they have achieved results which enable them to take the very town of Srebrenica." That's the first paragraph. You see that here, don't you: "The President of Republika Srpska is satisfied with the results of combat operations around Srebrenica and has agreed with the continuation of operations for the takeover of Srebrenica, disarming all Muslim terrorist gangs and complete demilitarisation of the Srebrenica enclave." That's the second paragraph. The third paragraph, you can follow it on the screen: "The President of Republika Srpska ordered that combat operations be continued, that full protection be ensured to UNPROFOR members and the Muslim civilian population and that they be guaranteed safety in the event that they cross over to the territory of Republika Srpska." That's the third paragraph. I thank the interpreters. I'm now reading the fourth paragraph: "In accordance with the order of the President of the Republika Srpska ... issuing an order to all combat units participating in combat operations around Srebrenica to ensure maximum protection and safety to all UNPROFOR members and the civilian Muslim population. ... order the subordinate units to refrain from destroying civilian targets unless they are forced to do so by strong enemy resistance. Forbid torching of residential buildings and treat ... civilian population and war prisoners in accordance with the Geneva Conventions of 12th August, 1949." Signed by assistant commander, Major-General Zdravko Tolimir. Thank you. I have read out this order and now tell me, please, were similar orders forwarded to you, namely that you should abide by the instructions issued by the Main Staff that no action be taken against civilians, that no houses be set on fire and that you act in accordance with the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I have said to you, the commander of our unit, Milorad Pelemis told us not to shoot at civilians and to direct them to go to the football pitch, which was in front of us, in Srebrenica. I don't remember him mentioning the Geneva Conventions, but the rest was along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, 4037 is this document on the OTP 65 ter list, and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D41, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Earlier while you were examined by the Prosecutor, we saw a document which was an order of the 10th Sabotage Detachment containing a list.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 04239 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch the rest.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. This is Exhibit P00233. All right, we have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: It says here: "Pursuant the order dated 10th of July." So this order that you received by Pelemis, was it written based on this other order, that I have just mentioned or was based on some other order?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know. I didn't see this order until last year, I think. But judging by the date, I think this is an order to the officers in Bijeljina, in the barracks, who were to be deployed from Bijeljina to Vlasenica and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the first time that I see this order myself because it was only admitted into evidence today. But I just asked you whether it was based on this order that you received your orders and instructions on how to comport yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just been told by my assistant, my legal assistant, that was this was already -- that this document has already been admitted into evidence. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now we're going move on to the events at the Branjevo farm. You said - and we have it on the transcript - that between 1.000 and 1500 -- or 1200 people were killed there, and that this is your free assessment. Did I quote you correctly or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this estimate just approximate or do you allow for this figure to be either smaller or larger?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't really say that this is the correct figure. I don't think it is bigger. It is possible that it is a smaller number but I can't really tell how many persons exactly were involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You said during the examination-in-chief that you refused to go to Zvornik or, to be more precise, to Pilica, where you were to kill some people at the cultural centre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A few people from my unit and I, myself, refused. We said that we didn't want to abide by that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. But you said also during the examination-in-chief that you were at a cafe near the cultural hall or culture centre in Pilica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Later on you said that you heard some shooting and that some 500 people were killed on that occasion, which is something that was being said while you were later on in Branjevo when you refused to participate in these events; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did not mention the 500 people. That figure, 500 individuals. It was mentioned by the lieutenant-colonel. And as for the shots and the hand-grenades explosions, I did hear that while we were still on the farm. We hadn't left the farm yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So you weren't an eye-witness to these events. You just mentioned, in fact, that you heard the blasts, the explosions; am I correct or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, afterwards when we left the cafe, when we left the farm, we could see, because there was a regiment of the police, that there were -- we could see some bodies outside the cultural hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you -- could you, yourself, make an estimate of how many bodies there were, or did you just say that, based on the words of that person?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I just repeated what this person in Branjevo said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Erdemovic, for your answers and for your evidence and thank you for coming to testify before this Trial Chamber today. I apologise for putting some questions that I wanted clarified for the benefit of the Trial Chamber and this trial. I thank you again, and I wish you a safe journey home to where you reside now. I don't want to mentioned name of that place. And I also would like to thank the interpreters for bearing with us because we were trying to finish with your testimony as fast as we could so that you could leave today because that was what you said your desire was. Thank you. I have completed my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tolimir, especially for your kind words. I think we should today mark the document 1D119 for identification, and we will come back to that for a decision.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D42 marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. And something else you used, the document 1D00133, do you tender that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey, do you have re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just two questions, two or three questions, Mr. President, and would you like to us write any motions or any support for my objection to that one document or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it is it not necessary to have written submissions. I just wanted to postpone the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, General Tolimir, on pages 71 and 72, reiterated Lieutenant Pelemis's admonition to the unit not to fire on any civilians. Yet you have testified that when a man in civilian clothes claiming he was civilian came into your group, Pelemis ordered that he be killed. How do you account for that difference?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I am not the one to explain that to you. I can't explain why he made that decision, why he took that decision. I don't know. But I also stated here that he had told us not to fire at civilians and then some -- an hour or an hour and a half later, he ordered Maljic to slit that man's throat. I cannot explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was that throat-cutting filmed by the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't really know that it was filmed by the 10th Sabotage Detachment, but I saw for the first time when you showed it to me yesterday and asked me whether there was the person involved and whether that was the place where this man was killed, I told you that I couldn't really tell, because -- but -- because I saw the mosque there, I said that I knew that there's a great chance that that was that person. Now, who filmed that, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did Kremenovic have a film of that person having his throat cut?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember precisely, but I think he did mention something but I can't speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this was not something that I questioned the witness about during my cross-examination. I apologise to Mr. McCloskey, but I would appreciate if he would confine his questions to the cross-examination. I apologise to the witness and thank him for his answers, but he cannot speak about things he didn't see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, could you give us a reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Mr. President. It was very clear to me, and I believe everyone in the courtroom, that General Tolimir was trying to count on Pelemis's order not to kill civilians as some sort of justification or some sort of defence that this didn't happen. As an officer of the court, I have reason to believe that -- and you've seen the evidence that he, in fact, ordered the murder of a man. And I have -- as an officer of the court, evidence that this was videotaped and kept by commanders of the 10th Sabotage Detachment as late as 1996 and that it was something that they had a record of indicating it would be something that they were proud of and wanted to keep for history. So this idea that there was a real order not to -- not kill people is totally undercut by their taking and holding this video of something being killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, do you want to put a question to this topic to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness clearly stated during the re-direct that he wasn't sure that that was the same person but that he saw the mosque, and based on that, he judged that perhaps this image actually related to that incident but he said that he couldn't tell that this was -- he didn't know whether this was actually videotaped by the 10th Sabotage Detachment. So I just pointed out what the witness had said, and I don't think that the witness should now be led to say things that he hadn't said before, and he said that he had seen it for the first time yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I take it you don't want to put another question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, can you direct us to today's transcript in cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: It's okay, Mr. McCloskey. I withdraw my attempt to have you point at the record where that issue was raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I can assure Your Honours, I do not deliberately ever go outside the scope of cross-examination. If I do wish to do so, I will ask you to reopen my re-direct, and I think you'll find that that is the reputation of this trial team and my directions are strict to all my trial team members. And I would like it if I could continue this witness to stay over till tomorrow so I can show him the documents that I'm referring to about this tape to help refresh his recollection, or in the very least, since there appears to be some question regarding the Prosecution on this, that I am able to show that material to you so that you understand I do have a reason to believe there is another tape, and I'm not talking about the piece of tape that we played, that was taped from the 12th of July. There was talk and statements of another tape that actually showed this killing, and I'm -- could show that to help refresh this witness's recollection, to clear up this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I think nobody is challenging the reputation of the Prosecution's team. Absolutely not. But sometimes we have to -- a discussion about on the rules of on re-examination. And therefore -- and perhaps you understood Judge Nyambe, she withdraw -- withdrew the -- the question she wanted to put to you. And, therefore, I think we are at the end of the questioning of this witness. The Chamber has no more questions for the witness, and I think perhaps Mr. Tolimir has an additional question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I was just about to say that in my cross-examination I never mentioned the event that Mr. McCloskey is now referring to. I just mentioned -- I asked the witness about the order issued by Mr. Pelemis, and I asked the witness whether Pelemis had said this in that sheltered area where they were, and there was nothing in the transcript where I mentioned anything or tried in any way to impute anything to Mr. McCloskey or anyone else, and least of all to the witness, because the witness told us everything he knew about this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, one answer of the witness to your question dealt with this order and the reality. I don't want to go into further details. And I think we are at a stage now to -- not to continue a discussion about this topic. We will find in -- in future occasions enough reasons for discussing the scope of cross and re-examination. I'm sure we will find a way to deal with it in the proper way. Mr. Erdemovic, will you be pleased to hear that this concludes your evidence and the questioning for you. The Chamber would like to thank you, that you were able to attend this trial and to come to The Hague again, and you may now return to your normal activities. Thank you very much again. The Court Officer will help you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are there any matters to raise? I think, especially, what is about the trial tomorrow and is there a witness available?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise for being a little sensitive and cranky at the end of the evening, and, Your Honour Nyambe, I apologise. Tomorrow we have spoken to Mr. Gajic, and we have Mr. Janc available for his continuing cross-examination, and I'm told that it may take some time so it should take the full day tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This seems to be convenient for you as well, Mr. Tolimir. Then we will have Mr. Janc as the next witness tomorrow. Thank you very much. We adjourn now and resume tomorrow in the afternoon, 2.15 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 18th day of May, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.,
